items.name: Flow
items.source_story_title: Animated ASCII Art for Web Pages
items.summary: Animated ASCII activity display for Claude Code and Pi; praised after installation.
items.why_included: An installed user's enthusiastic approval makes this more than an attractive demo.
items.evidence: conesus calls Flow gorgeous and says they installed it, while asking about contributing changes.

evidence_sources.author: conesus
evidence_sources.excerpt: Flow is gorgeous and fits this ascii art theme beautifully. I've installed it and have lots of changes I'd like to make.

items.name: Strands Decider 2B
items.source_story_title: Strands Decider 2B: a small, open-source, decision model
items.summary: Small open-source decision model; a browser user praises its email-classification speed and size.
items.why_included: A concrete on-device email-filtering use case supports the model's practical appeal.
items.evidence: miguelspizza reports running the model in a Chrome extension to filter email and praises its size, capability, and speed for bulk classification.

evidence_sources.author: miguelspizza
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is a great model. I've been running it on device in chrome extension to filter things like email. It is just the right mix of size, capability and speed to make it generally useful for adhoc bulk classification tasks.

items.name: Bigwords.page
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Bigwords.page – Turn any screen into a sign. The URL is the app
items.summary: Browser signs and countdowns encoded entirely in a shareable URL; no account needed.
items.why_included: Independent praise targets the URL-as-data design rather than merely the launch announcement.
items.evidence: whycome explicitly loves the design in which the URL contains all the data needed.

evidence_sources.author: whycome
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love solutions like this. Make the URL the entirety of the data needed. Awesome

items.name: Photopea
items.source_story_title: Tell HN: GitHub refuses to remove cracked copies of my software after a month
items.summary: Browser-based photo editor with layers and masks; multiple users praise hands-on editing.
items.why_included: Two independent users endorse the software despite the thread's focus on piracy.
items.evidence: randyrand praises Photopea as amazing software used frequently; Qwuke calls it a cool project after using it for small edits.

evidence_sources.author: randyrand
evidence_sources.excerpt: Wow, was not expecting this to be about Photopea! What an amazing piece of software I used it all the time! Less with AI these days, but still lots!

evidence_sources.author: Qwuke
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've used Photopea for small editing before, and even though it's not my daily driver, it's a really cool project.

items.name: Fixing Random
items.source_story_title: When random is not actually random enough
items.summary: Eric Lippert's programming series explores random-number pitfalls, distributions, weights, and noise.
items.why_included: A clear recommendation singles out a substantial learning resource rather than a bare reference.
items.evidence: wolfwyrd names Fixing Random, describes its breadth, and calls it a fantastic deep dive.

evidence_sources.author: wolfwyrd
evidence_sources.excerpt: There is a series of blog posts[0] by Eric Lippert called "Fixing Random"[1] that starts at random and covers distributions, weights, noise and so much more. It's a fantastic deep dive into the subject.

items.name: Darts, Dice, and Coins
items.source_story_title: When random is not actually random enough

items.evidence: colmmacc endorses Vose's alias method for sampling and calls Keith Schwarz's guide their favorite write-up.

evidence_sources.author: colmmacc
evidence_sources.excerpt: For sampling from a distribution, the best method is Vose's Alias. https://www.keithschwarz.com/darts-dice-coins/ is my favorite write up.
